title: JEPA & World Models
blurb: Predict the meaning, not the pixels. A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture learns by predicting the representation of a hidden part of the input from the rest. From the world-model blueprint, through images, video, audio, graphs and language, to the theory of why it works.

anchors.note: Lecture notes on the blueprint JEPA comes from: machines that learn world models, reason and plan. Read it for the why. LeCun's own position paper is on OpenReview, not arXiv.
I-JEPA, where it starts in practice. From one context block, predict the representations of other blocks of the same image: no pixel reconstruction, no hand-made augmentations.
MC-JEPA: one encoder learns both what is in a video and how it moves, joining optical flow with content features.
Graph-JEPA: the same idea for whole graphs, predicting the embedding of a masked subgraph with no positive or negative pairs.
A-JEPA: I-JEPA's recipe applied to audio spectrograms, with a curriculum for what to mask.
V-JEPA: video models trained only by predicting features, on 2 million videos. No pretrained image encoder, text, negatives or reconstruction.
Why predicting in embedding space differs from reconstructing pixels: in deep linear networks, JEPA training is biased toward high-influence features (strongly predictive ones), where an MAE is not.
A video JEPA that avoids representation collapse with variance and covariance regularisation.
V-JEPA 2: pretrained on over a million hours of internet video, then a small amount of robot data makes it a world model that plans actions.
LLM-JEPA: a first step to bring the embedding-space objective to language models, for finetuning and pretraining.
LeJEPA: what JEPA embeddings should look like (an isotropic Gaussian), and one regulariser, SIGReg, in place of the usual anti-collapse tricks. A single trade-off hyperparameter.
